hints: The y-axis is pH, not product directly. Look carefully at which line finishes lowest on the graph after the same time.
Remember the stem says product causes pH to fall, so biggest pH fall means most product. Think about why 37 C works better than 75 C for a human-type enzyme.
walkthrough:
**Link pH to product**

Think like a detective. We cannot see product, but we can see pH.

The question tells us: more product = lower pH. So the curve that drops the furthest has made the most product.

**Read the four curves**

Look at the right-hand end of the graph, where time is greatest.

The lowest pH (steepest, bottom line) is the solid line. From the key, that is non-immobilised, $37^{\circ}C$. The highest pH (least drop) is the top dashed line, non-immobilised, $75^{\circ}C$.

**Make biological sense of it**

At $37^{\circ}C$, close to optimum, the enzyme keeps its shape and works fast, so lots of acidic product forms.

At $75^{\circ}C$, the free enzyme denatures quickly, so very little product forms. Immobilisation gives some heat stability, which is why immobilised at $75^{\circ}C$ does a little better than free at $75^{\circ}C$, but still worse than at $37^{\circ}C$.

options.A: Good second choice, it drops to a low pH, but its dotted line finishes just above the solid line, so it made slightly less product.
options.B: At 75 C even immobilised enzyme is well above optimum, so pH falls only a little, showing low yield.
options.C: The solid line falls furthest to the lowest pH, showing the greatest accumulation of acidic product, so highest yield.
options.D: This top dashed line shows the smallest pH fall, so the free enzyme at 75 C has denatured and made the least product.
